article.name: AutoBot
article.summary: AutoBot is a self-hosted AI platform whose memory is split across general SQLite memory, durable PostgreSQL knowledge facts and their Redis/vector projections, a Redis-backed graph, and conversation-derived trajectory and verbatim stores. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

who_what.text: The public repository is under GitHub account mrveiss. Its README describes AutoBot as a self-hosted AI platform with chat, a RAG knowledge base, knowledge graph, LLM gateway, management layer and installable modules; it is a platform and service stack rather than a standalone memory library.

architecture.text: General memory uses a SQLite memory_entries table with category, content, JSON metadata, timestamp, reference path, embedding and required user_id. Task history is a distinct record with lifecycle, timing, agent, input/output, error and relationship fields.

Knowledge facts are persisted through the fact store before Redis and ChromaDB projections. The source identifies the PostgreSQL knowledge_facts row as authoritative; vectorization status and reconciliation state are tracked separately from the durable fact.

Conversation turns feed background verbatim and fact-extraction tasks, with a separate trajectory-capture path. Graph entities/relations, Redis working memory, vector trajectories and verbatim chunks are separate lanes with separate interfaces and scope rules.

behavior.text: General-memory writes require a nonblank user_id and reject the reserved legacy owner for new writes; reads and deletes use owner-scoped predicates. Fact writes sanitize content/metadata, attach provenance defaults and identifiers, persist the durable row, then update Redis and ChromaDB projections.

Fact updates merge sanitized metadata and changed content into the durable row before refreshing projections. Fact deletion removes the durable row first and then cleans Redis mappings and the Chroma vector; vector-store deletion errors are logged. Chat turn completion enqueues verbatim writes and fact extraction asynchronously.

Retrieval is multi-lane: general-memory search; knowledge search with vector/lexical/hybrid components and permission-aware filters; an Essential Story scan capped at 200 facts with principal filtering and a model token budget; trajectory similarity search with reward filtering and optional tenant/user predicates; and separate verbatim retrieval.

The memory privacy API enumerates verbatim, trajectory, working-memory, graph, retrieval-learner and general stores. The knowledge-fact store is not in that set, so this operation is not a single complete erase across every memory lane.

metrics.evidence: Multiple retrieval lanes and a bounded essential-fact prompt context are visible in source. No answerability or abstention workload was run.
Fact update and verification/quarantine paths are present. No correction accuracy or stale-value probes were run.
Fact deletion and six-store privacy handling are visible, but the latter omits knowledge facts; no residual-copy probes were run.
Required owner/principal filters exist in multiple lanes; no cross-user or cross-tenant isolation workload was run.
Facts carry provenance fields and chat can return citations; no source-support adjudication was performed.
Background enqueues, trajectory query timing and vectorization status are source-visible; no latency or delay measurements were collected.
Essential-story token budgets and memory monitoring/counters exist in source; no memory-attributed token, cost or storage measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of selected documentation and code at one verified head. It does not establish end-to-end correctness, citation quality, complete deletion across backups or every store, partial-projection behavior in production, cross-tenant isolation across every route, latency, or reliability under load.
Each lane has distinct mutation, retention, scope and provenance behavior. In particular, the privacy forget-everywhere operation covers six listed stores and not the knowledge-fact store.
The benchmark and runtime outcomes remain unknown because AutoBot, benchmark workloads and tests were not run for this review.
